entries.title: Expanding the Google AI Professional Certificate with vibe coding
entries.content:
Whether you are taking your very first step into AI or looking to build custom tools for your team, our goal with the Google AI Professional Certificate has stayed the same: helping you learn how to make AI work for you. Since launching in February, it has become the most popular generative AI certificate of all time on Coursera. 1 Millions of people have learned to put AI to work with our AI curriculum, 2 while leading employers like Deloitte, Verizon, Lyft, and Walmart are using the course to train their teams.

But AI moves fast, and we are committed to keeping our curriculum just as dynamic. Lately, our learners have been asking for deeper lessons on vibe coding: describing what you want in everyday language while AI handles the technical code to build and deploy your app. This interest reflects a broader trend, with U.S. search for vibe coding up by 140% on average versus last year. 3

Our newest vibe coding course launches today. This course helps everyone become a builder, creating robust, shareable apps. We teach you how to plan, test and debug, and deploy your app, turning your best ideas into practical tools. Whether it's building a custom team dashboard, automating a workflow, or building a customer intake tool, no coding experience is required.

We love seeing what people are building. Take former Walmart truck driver turned Logistics Load Manager Leo Garcia in Bentonville, Arkansas. Using what he learned in the Google AI Professional Certificate, Leo used an internal tool to design four custom applications to optimize operations across several states. One of his apps, "Get My Driver Home," condensed daily reporting meetings into 15-minute huddles. His app now coordinates shifts for drivers, and Walmart continues to review associate created apps like Leo’s, showing what is possible when you give people the tools and confidence to solve their own challenges.

We are also seeing companies put this training to work in other practical, everyday ways. Verizon is offering the Google AI Professional Certificate to help its workforce build AI fluency. Recent graduates are applying their skills to daily work projects, moving from basic email drafting to building highly customized tools like virtual quoting assistants in Gemini Notebook. By equipping employees with tools and skills, Verizon is empowering its workforce to solve everyday challenges directly within their roles.

“Empowering our workforce and our communities with AI fluency has been a core priority for Verizon. We have been thrilled to offer the Google AI Professional Certificate to our Verizon Small Business customers, Verizon Small Business Digital Ready program users, current management Verizon employees, as well as former employees of Verizon through our Reskilling and Career Transition Fund,” said Donna Epps, Chief Responsible Business Officer of Verizon. “This training has played a key role in helping us deliver more dynamic experiences for the communities we serve and adding these new vibe coding resources will only enhance our impact.”

By expanding our curriculum to include practical skills like vibe coding, we’re continuing our commitment to make AI accessible, relevant, and useful for everyone. Whether you’re streamlining logistics at a multinational company or designing a custom app for your team, the Google AI Professional Certificate is built to help you make AI work for you.

Enroll today to get started: grow.google/AICert

entries.title: Have more fun at the state fair with these Google tools
entries.summary: New state fair food Google search
entries.content:
With Search interest in “state fair new food” skyrocketing 600% in the last month, it’s clear people are gearing up for one of America’s favorite traditions. Whether you’re hoping to taste iconic foods-on-a-stick, spend your day at the livestock show, catch some live music, or do a little of everything, your state fair day will surely be packed full of things to do.

To help you get the most out of every moment (and every bite), we’re sharing five easy ways Google’s tools can help you make plans, explore, and create memories at the state fair.

1. Create your perfect itinerary.

Spend less time planning your route and more time making memories. Just give Gemini your wishlist — concerts, farm exhibits, shaded breaks — and who you’re bringing along. In seconds, you’ll get a tailored schedule with built-in rest stops designed to maximize the fun and save your feet.

2. Take the stress out of getting there and getting around.

Skip the hassle of unexpected driving delays and find what you need on the go. Use real-time information in Ask Maps, our Gemini-powered conversational feature in Google Maps, to check for any incidents or delays on your route before you leave so you don't miss your favorite activities. You can even use Ask Maps to find what you need on-site, like a place to charge your phone or fill up your water bottle.

3. Discover the best treats.

The state fair is all about food — think deep-fried classics like corn dogs, and endless sweet treats. (It’s no surprise “new fair foods 2026” is a breakout search!)

Use AI Mode in Search to discover the top-rated foods-on-a-stick at your local state fair or ask about the best gluten free options. You’ll see a range of top options, helping you skip the guesswork so you can easily find what you’re looking for.

4. Ask questions about things you see.

Spot something interesting at the fairgrounds? Satisfy your curiosity in real time with Gemini Live or Search Live. Just tap the Live icon and point your camera at an exhibit — like Iowa’s famous butter sculpture — to ask about its history. You can even aim your lens at a crowded fair map to quickly find the nearest cool-down zone.

5. Turn photos into legendary keepsakes.

Snap a picture of yourself enjoying a funnel cake and ask Gemini to render it as a vintage 1950s postcard. Or take a photo of the rodeo arena and ask Gemini to place you in the center of the action as a championship bull rider. All it takes is a photo and a little imagination to create memorable and sharable content that captures the fun of the day.

Google is excited to visit state fairs this summer! Swing by the Gemini Visitor Centers at the state fairs in Iowa (August 13-15), Minnesota (August 27-29), or Texas (October 9-10) to try this out for yourself.

entries.title: Evolve your marketing with new AI tools
entries.summary: Advisor UI in Google Ads and Google Analytics
entries.content:
Great marketing has always required deep measurement expertise to uncover the "why" and strategic agility to execute the "how." That’s why we introduced Ask Advisor 1 — our in-product AI agent across Google’s marketing platforms — to put those answers and actions directly into marketers' hands.

Today, we’re announcing new agentic capabilities across Google Ads and Google Analytics designed to amplify your expertise, helping you uncover insights faster, make smarter business decisions, and stay firmly in the driver’s seat as you chart your path to growth.

Spot opportunities faster with new homepage insights

It’s critical for analyst teams to stay on top of performance shifts as they happen. Google Analytics now makes this easier than ever, with new AI Overviews at the top of the homepage that give you an instant summary of important updates since you last logged in. From seasonal peaks in sales to changes in traffic, you can quickly understand what matters right now, and more importantly, what you should do about it.

When a data card catches your eye, a single click carries that context straight into Ask Advisor to analyze further. And now, you can stay up to date with these smart summaries at your own pace by opting into notifications via phone or email at a frequency that suits you.

We’ve also revamped the Google Ads homepage to surface timely AI-powered insights cards personalized to your business 1 . You now have the context you need to confidently adjust your strategy, ensuring you capture new demand the moment it appears. Want to understand how competitors are impacting your impression share or what trends could improve your campaigns? Use the prompt box above the insights cards to generate a custom insight based on what’s top of mind.

Become a data expert with new visual reporting

When it's time to evaluate your performance, reporting should be intuitive and easy. With the new Dashboards 1 in Google Ads (coming soon in Google Analytics), you can transform raw data into clear visualizations with simple text prompts. Every report automatically generates a real-time summary explaining the "why" behind the data, helping you easily understand your performance or make a case for a new campaign idea.

Benchmark your success

It’s always important to identify where you have room to grow. Now, you can dig even deeper into your campaign performance in Google Analytics with Ask Advisor. We’re introducing a new benchmarking feature that compares your campaign performance against anonymized averages from similar businesses, helping you refine your strategy with confidence.

"Ask Advisor has become my go-to for a directional check on paid media performance… That speed matters because it gives me time to dig deeper and make shifts that improve performance sooner."

— Kevin Marshall, Paid Media Director at Gardyn

Built with Gemini, these new solutions will help marketers move from insight to action even faster. Get started today in Google Ads and Google Analytics.

entries.title: Venmo is giving you a new way to pay on Google Play.
entries.summary: Venmo is now available as a payment option on Google Play, giving you more flexibility at checkout.
entries.content:
Venmo is now available as a payment option on Google Play, giving you more flexibility at checkout. Starting today, you can link your Venmo account to the Google Play Store to bring the digital wallet you already trust to the apps, games and digital content you love most.

Whether you use your Venmo balance or a linked payment method, you’ll have a new way to level up in your favorite games, manage your subscriptions and tip the creators who inspire you.

It’s the secure, fast, and social experience you know, now ready to use across Google Play. To update the way you pay on Play, go to your payment methods in the Google Play Store to link your Venmo account.

entries.title: See what 5 builders are making with Gemini Omni
entries.content:
At this year’s I/O, we introduced Gemini Omni Flash, our first model in the new Omni family. Omni makes creating and editing videos as easy as having a conversation. You can generate high-quality videos from text, image, video, or audio references, and even edit your own videos. And since Omni combines an intuitive understanding of physics with Gemini’s real-world knowledge, it creates more realistic outputs.

We recently gave developers access to Omni, and builders have already used it for a range of projects. Here are some of the demos that caught our eye.

Switch angles and perspectives.

Omni makes editing videos incredibly easy. You can change camera angles, switch environments, and apply cinematic zooms — all without losing the thread of your original scene.

Builder Leon Lin (@LexnLin on X) took full advantage of this capability, capturing a woman standing in the middle of a city from about 20 different perspectives. You see her from every angle imaginable: up close and far away, head on and in profile, from above, and from below. Some shots zoom in, while others hold still. And the background shifts: She stands on sidewalks, crosswalks, and city streets, surrounded by pedestrians, cars, trams, and a range of different buildings.

Transform the world around you.

Omni lets you change what’s happening in a video and create something you never could have filmed yourself. You can edit the action or swap in different objects, and Omni will still maintain a coherent, cohesive scene.

Take this video from builder Carlos Santana (@DotCSV on X), for example. He changes an outdoor scene using only his voice, switching the lighting from day to night, adding cloudy skies and rainy sounds, turning the leaves orange, and covering the ground in snow.

Animate everyday objects.

With Omni in Google Flow, you can turn sketches into realistic videos, using doodles to guide how individual elements move. And you can decide whether these hand-drawn elements become part of your final product.

Builder Pan (@sebatheepan on X), for instance, uses doodles to playfully transform everyday objects. A lemon becomes a submarine bobbing in the ocean. A cup of espresso is now a hot air balloon transporting someone through the sky. A pair of hot peppers form a sleeping dragon that breathes fire when startled. A match is recast as a rocket ship. And scissors turn into a scary shark looking for a snack.

Play with different styles or visual effects.

Curious what your video would look like with a completely different aesthetic? With Omni, you can change styles and apply effects to create something that matches your vision. Define the look you want by inputting references, or just describe what you’re looking for in natural language. Omni blends that together to create a cohesive clip.

Builder Jerrod Lew (@jerrod_lew on X) put this to the test with Omni in Google Flow, rendering a video of a woman walking down the street in four different animation styles. The original clip fluidly shifts from live-action to anime to claymation and more, never interrupting the woman’s natural forward progression.

Bring ideas to life.

The team at Hyperagent (@hyperagentapp on X) used Omni to visualize three different concepts with video. They layered landscaping into a video of an empty park to create a before-and-after design proposal. They personified data with an animated professor who explains business dashboards. And they gamified a to-do list with a video showing a character clearing tasks.

Omni blends knowledge with creativity, letting you create scenes that follow real-world logic. Try it in the Gemini app, Google Flow, Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, or the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.

entries.title: How Gemini plans such detailed vacation itineraries for you
entries.content:
Planning a trip can feel like a second job. Between hunting down flight confirmations, mapping distances between destinations, and scrolling through countless restaurant reviews, the logistics quickly stack up. Gemini can take some of that work off your plate, helping you organize custom vacations with less stress. All you need to do is ask.

Gemini doesn’t just browse the web — it connects directly to Google Maps, Hotels, and Flights to build highly personalized itineraries based on real-world data and your specific preferences. Here’s what happens behind the scenes when you ask it for help planning a trip, whether you’re brainstorming options or finalizing bookings.

Gathering real-time data

Let’s say you’re taking a trip to Kyoto later this year. You need flights, hotels, and restaurant reservations — plus stuff to do while you’re there. Gemini first tackles this challenge by tapping into Google’s ecosystem for accurate, real-world data.

Gemini gets real-time information — think locations, reviews, prices, and more — from Google Maps, Flights, and Hotels. It also pulls visual inspiration and recommendations from YouTube creators. And if you call on the Viator app while you’re in Gemini, it can even help you explore and book expertly curated travel tours, activities, and excursions.

Finding the best recommendations

Gemini then pairs that Google Search data with advanced AI to give you custom travel recommendations.

Gemini uses the context you’ve provided in your prompt — including basics, like your destination and travel dates, or specifics, like that you’re looking for hidden-gem brunch spots near the train station. And if you toggle on Personal Intelligence in Google apps — like Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube — Gemini can proactively factor in your interests, preferences, and constraints.

With Personal Intelligence, Gemini securely connects the dots across your Google apps, past chats, and custom instructions. It can make personalized suggestions, like restaurants to try based on food pictures you’ve saved to Google Photos or travel videos you’ve searched on YouTube. It can also reference plans you’ve already booked using flight details, hotel confirmations, and restaurant reservations in your Gmail.

If you ask Gemini to remember your interests and past picks, it can help you find new favorites fine-tuned to your tastes. It can even identify patterns across your Google apps to recommend your next perfect travel destination.

Building your itinerary

Gemini understands how different trip requirements — like locations, travel times, existing plans, and personal preferences — intersect. So when you ask it to build an itinerary, it creates a cohesive plan that accounts for all your constraints.

Gemini can create custom routes and group things to do by neighborhood. And with Personal Intelligence, it can build your itinerary around your existing plans and preferences — cross-referencing times and locations before weaving things into your schedule.

Gemini Spark, your 24/7 personal AI agent, can also make sense of your inbox — turning messy trip-planning email chains into a clear master plan. Ask it to monitor your Gmail, and as items related to your trip (like booked tours, flights, and hotels) pop up, it works in the background — automatically building out a Google Doc with your travel itinerary.

Finalizing the details

Gemini doesn’t stop at building itineraries. It can handle the heavy lifting and help you finalize the details of your trip.

Gemini Spark, for example, can help with mundane tasks, like comparing rental cars or drafting a packing list. It handles the research, saving you the tedium of juggling multiple tabs or obsessively checking the weather. When it’s done, it suggests the best choices and lets you make the final decision.

Gemini Spark can also even use Chrome to navigate to your favorite airline’s site, search for flights, and start filling in your booking information — handing the task back over to you, so all you have to do is press “book.” It can also help you find and book travel accommodations and manage dining reservations. And if you give it access, it can email your finalized itinerary to your travel crew so everyone knows the plan.

entries.title: Parents can now send money to their kids on Google Wallet.
entries.summary: U.S. parents can set up a secure digital balance on Google Wallet for their kids to tap and pay using Android and Wear OS devices.
entries.content:
With back-to-school season fast approaching, parents are busy preparing their children for the year ahead. To make getting ready a little easier, today we're launching a new Google Wallet tool that gives parents a safe and simple way to manage their kids' money, building on the helpful features we already offer to families.

Now parents in the U.S. can set up a secure balance on Google Wallet for their children and teens under 18. In an increasingly cashless world, kids can tap to pay with Google Pay in stores using their NFC-enabled Android or Wear OS devices.

As a parent, you have full control of their balance and activity through Family Link. You can easily transfer money directly from your own account, and soon you'll be able to schedule automated regular payments. You can also set specific spending limits and track transactions in real time. And if needed, you can lock or unlock the balance instantly. It's a practical way to teach children smart money habits and give them independence, all without needing to open a bank account.

entries.title: Our WeatherNext 2 AI model demonstrated a massive leap forward in predicting cyclones.
entries.summary: Google DeepMind’s WeatherNext 2 shows state-of-the-art accuracy in cyclone prediction.
entries.content:
Predicting how hurricanes and cyclones develop is a longstanding challenge, and every hour of warning counts. Tropical cyclones are among the most destructive weather events on Earth, and for meteorologists, issuing accurate, timely warnings is a constant race against time.

Today, in a paper published in Nature, Google researchers show that our WeatherNext AI model achieved state-of-the-art accuracy in predicting a cyclone's track, intensity, and wind structure. This represents a massive leap forward — roughly a decade of meteorological progress in one model.

To help build climate resilience worldwide, we are now open-sourcing the WeatherNext 2 model to the global research community. For more information, check the Google DeepMind blog.

entries.title: Step into the world of tango on Google Arts & Culture
entries.content:
Journey into the heart of one of Argentina’s most passionate and iconic cultural treasures: tango. Through a new collection on Google Arts & Culture, we’re bringing the history, music, and spirit of tango to users around the world.

Google Arts & Culture has long been committed to preserving and celebrating Argentina’s rich heritage, having collaborated with 25 local partners across the country. Following the success of Argentina’s Table — our exploration of the nation’s diverse culinary scene — we’re now turning our focus to the dance and music style that’s captivated global audiences and earned a place on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

In collaboration with five key partners — MALBA (Museo de Arte Latinoamericano de Buenos Aires Malba), Tango & Tango, The National Secretariat of Culture of Argentina, the Ministry of Culture of the City of Buenos Aires, and Marca País Argentina — we’ve brought together over 50 stories, not just about the dance, but about the people who keep it alive. Visit the collection to explore the legacies of legends like Carlos Gardel and Julio De Caro, as well as the personal stories of contemporary orchestra players, passionate dancers, and the artisans who craft the instruments and shoes that define the tango style.

"In the national government, we celebrate initiatives like this, which combine technology, cooperation between institutions, and coordination with the private sector to preserve and disseminate our cultural heritage," says Leonardo Cifelli, Argentina's national secretary of culture. "A few weeks away from a new anniversary of tango’s UNESCO recognition (September 30), this collaboration represents a new opportunity to project one of the most valuable expressions of Argentine identity to the world."

Born in the barrios: Tango rose from humble beginnings to global fame. Its journey reflects Argentina's own evolution, embracing both its heritage and its future. This cultural weight that ultimately led to tango’s 2009 inclusion on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list, cementing its place as a pillar of global identity despite ongoing debates over its institutionalization.

The legends of tango: The genre was shaped by iconic master musicians like Carlos Gardel, Ástor Piazzolla, Aníbal Troilo, Julio De Caro and other tango figures, whose enduring legacies still define the rhythm and soul of the music today.

A global heartbeat in Buenos Aires: A powerful global attraction, tango brings people from all corners of the world to the streets of Buenos Aires, uniting a passionate international community. Discover how this comes to life throughout the city by exploring tango neighborhoods and learning about the historic traditions of tango bars.

Whether you’re a seasoned milonguero or discovering tango for the first time, we hope this project inspires you to step into the history, movement and soul of Argentina on the dedicated page and by downloading the free Google Arts & Culture app on iOS or Android.

entries.title: Ask Maps gets more helpful with food ordering and more
entries.content:
Ask Maps is Google Maps’ biggest transformation in over a decade. By bringing Gemini model capabilities together with the world’s freshest map, we’ve made it easier than ever to get answers to real-world questions.

We’ve been thrilled to see how Ask Maps is helping people use Maps in entirely new ways — from finding a restaurant with great vibes that’s still quiet enough for conversation to mapping out a scenic three-hour motorcycle ride. Building on this, we’re now making Ask Maps even more helpful with new agentic capabilities, real-time transit information, Personal Intelligence, and conversational contributions so you can get more done. It’s also rolling out in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Indonesia, Japan, and Mexico, along with over 150 countries and territories in English.

Order food, find the perfect hotel, and discover events.

Ask Maps can now handle complex, multi-step tasks for you using new agentic capabilities. If you want to order takeout before leaving the office, just ask Maps to “order spicy pad kee mao with seafood for me to pick up on my way home.” It’ll find open restaurants along your route that serve what you're craving and can even consider things like your saved places or specific dietary needs. Once you select a restaurant, Ask Maps can automatically add the dish you’re looking for directly to your cart so you can easily review and complete your order. Food ordering is rolling out now with partners like Square and Toast, with Uber Eats coming soon. We’ll continue to evolve these experiences as we co-develop the Universal Commerce Protocol for Food with partners.

With Ask Maps, you can also quickly discover the latest information about hotels and local events. Ask for what you need: “For next week’s conference in downtown Miami, find me a decently priced, top-rated hotel with an artsy vibe, within walking distance from a gym and restaurants.” Ask Maps compares real-time prices and checks availability for you so you can find the right spot. And if you need ideas for what to do nearby, Ask Maps will show you everything from concerts to comedy shows, complete with links for tickets.

Get personalized answers and resume past conversations.

With Personal Intelligence, you can choose to securely connect Ask Maps to Gmail, and soon other apps like Calendar. Ask Maps automatically factors in your upcoming flight or dinner reservations, giving you relevant suggestions without you having to explain your existing plans. For example, if you’re traveling, try asking: “Give me ideas on how to spend a few hours near the hotel before my flight tomorrow.” You'll see nearby recommendations based on your hotel reservation in Gmail — along with tips for getting to the airport afterwards, like what time to leave.

With Personal Intelligence in Ask Maps, you’re in control — connecting to your Gmail is off by default and you decide if you want to connect. Personal Intelligence is built with privacy in mind, and you can learn more about our approach here.

If your history settings are turned on, Ask Maps also remembers past conversations so you can pick up where you left off. Simply ask, “Remind me, what activities did you suggest for my trip to Seattle?” Maps will instantly pull up your previous ideas so you don't have to start planning from scratch.

Get trusted, real-time transit information instantly.

Ask Maps already gives you helpful, real-time information — like what traffic to expect on your morning commute or if there’s construction or an accident along the way. You can even check how busy a shop or restaurant is before you head out so you can avoid waiting in long lines. Now, we’re bringing these live updates to transit. A new transit widget right in Ask Maps keeps you informed about up-to-the-minute delays for your bus, train, subway, or ferry ride. So if you ask, “Is there a ferry to get to Taronga Zoo with views of the Opera House?” you’ll see all of your options at a glance on a virtual departure board. If a ferry is running late, the wait adjusts in real-time — updating minute by minute — so you know exactly when to head to the dock.

Tell Maps about updates and share tips conversationally

Insights from over 500 million contributors play a big role in keeping Maps fresh and helpful, and now we’re making it simpler to share updates. You can suggest edits conversationally, right from Ask Maps and the Contribute tab. You can even upload a photo of a storefront sign — Maps will detect the new hours from the image, and ask you to confirm before submitting the suggestion for you. As always, Maps’ built-in protection systems review suggested edits for accuracy, and won’t post suggestions that violate our policies. It’s also easy to tell Maps about an insider tip — just say something like “more parking is available behind the building,” and Ask Maps will surface this helpful information to others in the community.

The live transit widget, more personalized responses, and remembering past conversations in Ask Maps are rolling out now everywhere Ask Maps is available. Food ordering, discovering hotels and events, and conversational contributions are rolling out now in the U.S., with more countries to come over time. With these updates, we hope Ask Maps makes navigating your day just a little easier.
